content:
sam: FYI customer reported 401 + module/tag confusion when pulling our Go SDK v2 release. Ticket #5278.

sam: Repro steps they gave:
```
module example.com/acmeapp

go 1.20

require github.com/redwood/inference-go v2.0.0
```
They run `go get github.com/redwood/inference-go@v2.0.0` and get: `invalid version: unknown revision v2.0.0`.

maria: Do we have the repo module path set to `/v2` in the tagged tree? If the module line inside go.mod is `module github.com/redwood/inference-go` then modules >v1 will break.

sam: Here's the snippet from the customer's `go.mod` plus the error logs they pasted:
```
$ go get github.com/redwood/inference-go@v2.0.0
go: github.com/redwood/inference-go@v2.0.0: invalid version: unknown revision v2.0.0
```

eli: Quick checklist:
- Verify repo has a git tag `v2.0.0` on the release commit.
- Verify `go.mod` at that tag has `module github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2` (required for major v2+).
- Check `git ls-remote --tags origin` to confirm tag exists.

maria: I pulled the repo at `v2.0.0` locally — the tag exists but the go.mod inside tag is `module github.com/redwood/inference-go` (no /v2). That explains `unknown revision` + `+incompatible` behavior. Go treats the tag as incompatible unless module path matches.

jess: Oof. Customer already on prod and can't upgrade. Any short-term workaround for them?

eli: Workarounds: 
- Pin to the last v1.x.x tag (e.g., `go get github.com/redwood/inference-go@v1.9.3`) if that meets their needs.
- Use a pseudo-version pointing to a commit (e.g., `require github.com/redwood/inference-go v0.0.0-20240102030405-abcdef123456`), but that's messy.
- Locally `replace` in their `go.mod` to point at a fork that has `module .../v2` until we publish a fixed tag:
```
replace github.com/redwood/inference-go => github.com/acme/fork/inference-go v2.0.0
```
That requires them to host a fork or we cut a temporary branch.

maria: Long-term fix: we need to cut a new v2 tag where go.mod module line is `github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2`. Two options:
1) Update module path in tree, tag `v2.0.1` with same codebase (breaking source backwards compatibility for import paths).
2) If we don't want to change import paths, we should not use v2 in the tag and publish as v1.* (but semver semantics discourage that).

sam: Customer asked if we can publish a compatibility release today. Can release team do a patch that updates module path and pushes v2.0.1?

release-bot: @release-team new release request created: RQ-1024 — add `/v2` to module path and push v2.0.1 tag. Priority=high.

jess: For immediate support I'll send them step-by-step to pin to v1.9.3 and open a ticket explaining the upcoming v2.0.1. Also ask them to set `GOPRIVATE` if they're using private mirrors.

eli: Additional notes for engineering: when cutting major-version tags we must: 
- Update `module` line to include `/vN` (N>=2).
- Run `gofmt`/`go list`/`go mod tidy` and test importing from another module.
- Add release notes explaining break and migration path.

maria: After we push v2.0.1 with module path fixed, customers should run `go get github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2@v2.0.1` and update imports to `github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2` if they want to adopt v2.

sam: I'll update the ticket and ping customer. Thanks — I'll keep this thread updated with release status. :thumbsup:

jess: +1. Please include repro commands I can paste into the ticket.

sam: Repro commands for ticket:
```
# verify tag exists
git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/redwood/inference-go.git

# try to pull v2
go get github.com/redwood/inference-go@v2.0.0

# show go version and env
go version
go env GOPROXY GOPRIVATE
```

maria: I'll coordinate the v2.0.1 tag and post back here with the new tag hash. :shipit:

release-bot: RQ-1024 assigned to @maria. ETA 4h.

sam: closing loop in ticket and will update customer once tag is live.
